sourceTitle: Goodman service manual RS6621003r3 (June 2020), 80% single-stage gas furnaces GMES80, AMES80, GCES80, ACES80, VMES80 and VCES80, troubleshooting chart
safetyNote: If you smell gas, do not touch any electrical switch or use a phone in the building; leave immediately and call your gas supplier from outside. Turn off electrical power at the furnace switch or breaker before opening any panel, and never bypass or jumper a limit, rollout or pressure switch. Gas valve, burner, venting, wiring and control-board work should be done by a licensed HVAC technician.
displayPattern: Diagnostic LED through the blower-door window on an 80% single-stage *MES80 or *CES80 furnace: Goodman GMES80 and GCES80, Amana AMES80 and ACES80, GMC VMES80 and VCES80. Count the flashes between pauses. This is not the 7-segment EE display on a 90%+ furnace.
meaning: Primary or auxiliary limit circuit is open. The circulator blower runs and the furnace does not heat.
causes: Faulty primary or auxiliary limit switch
Not enough air over the heat exchanger: blocked filters, restrictive ductwork, the wrong circulator speed, or a failed circulator blower
diySteps: Turn the furnace off and replace a dirty air filter. Open supply and return grilles that are closed
The abnormal-operation section names the same airflow causes: a dirty filter, duct resistance, a faulty limit, a faulty blower, or blower speed set too low
Technician: check the limit, circulator speed and performance, and the limit-circuit wiring. Do not jumper the limit
proAdvice: Call a licensed HVAC technician if four flashes returns after the filter is clean and the grilles are open. Six flashes on this chart is the rollout switch or a blown control fuse, which is a different shutdown. This chart is service manual RS6621003r3 for those 80% single-stage models. A 7-segment code such as EE0 or EE2 is a different furnace family.
